candidate.title: Instance-wide shared webhook secret allows overwriting any user's app credentials (no per-user binding/replay protection)
reports: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — a single global webhook secret authorizes credential create/overwrite for any userid, so one leaked secret compromises every user's app credentials

inbound credential webhook relies only on a shared secret with no per-request signature, replay protection, per-user/per-app scoping, or rate limiting, allowing anyone with the secret to overwrite any user's credentials

[bug] the webhook accepts an arbitrary userid and appslug and overwrites that user's stored credential key with attacker-supplied decrypted json without any check that the key matches the app's expected credential schema. anyone holding the single shared calcomwebhooksecret (one secret for all apps and all users, no per-caller scoping) can replace any user's app credential with arbitrary keys of the wrong shape; downstream calendarservice code then reads undefined fields from the key and every booking for that user fails, with no audit trail distinguishing webhook-written credentials from oauth-written ones.
candidate.example: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — a single global webhook secret authorizes credential create/overwrite for any userid, so one leaked secret compromises every user's app credentials

fix_scope: minimal fix for the demonstrated instance only

sibling_instances.note: other instances of this class are unverified siblings; fix.patch does not address them

claim_restated: The webhook must not allow a caller who knows a single instance-wide secret to create or overwrite credentials for an arbitrary target userId.
expected_failure: Instance-wide shared webhook secret should NOT authorize overwriting another user's app credentials

labels: Instance-wide static webhook secret authorizes credential writes for arbitrary userid/appslug
No replay/event-identity/version guard permits stale or concurrent credential overwrites
multi_defect.explanation: Most findings describe broken authorization scoping via a shared global secret, while others describe missing replay/versioning controls that allow stale or concurrent overwrites; these have different root causes and fixes.
multi_defect.status: the promoted verdict verifies ONE of these defects; the other(s) are unverified extras
